title: Claims manifest for a contribution note
description: One record per claim of a stand-alone note: what is asserted, with what standing, resting on what, reproducible how, and by whom. The vocabulary of standing is the project's: see the method note. A manifest is a projection of the project's log, written so that a reader, human or machine, can take a claim without the history.

note.description: The note's slug; the claim identifiers are prefixed by it.

version.description: The note revision this manifest describes, as an ISO date or a tag.

doi.description: DOI of the archived release of this version, when one exists.

text.description: SPDX identifier for the note's text, e.g. CC-BY-4.0.

authors.description: Human authors. Model contributions are recorded per claim under provenance.

summary.description: A few sentences for a reader deciding whether to open the note.

open_problems.description: Claim identifiers (in this or another manifest) whose status is open or conjecture and which the note presents as the targets.

id.description: note-slug/claim-slug. Stable across revisions of the note even if the note's numbering changes.

kind.description: negative-result: a route shown not to work, recorded so it is not retried. certificate-campaign: a family of machine-checked proofs on named cells.

label.description: How the note names it in this version, e.g. 'Theorem 1 (the reduction)'.

gist.description: One short sentence saying what the claim asserts, for a reader who does not know the note's names; shown beside the label in the index. Plain language, LaTeX only where unavoidable.

statement.description: The statement in plain language with LaTeX where needed. Self-contained enough to be read without the note; terms defined in the note are named, not explained.

status.description: proved: a written argument read by an independent checker with its own programs. proved-unchecked: a written argument with no second reader. certified: a machine-checked proof object (DRAT, LRAT, a CPOG-certified count, Lean, Isabelle) on the cells named in scope. solver: a SAT or LP verdict on named cells without a checked proof object. computed: an exact computation with no solver verdict. explored: floating-point or sampled evidence only. conjecture: believed, with evidence named. open: a target with no verdict. closed-route: a method shown not to reach the target. corrected: a statement of an earlier version repaired here. refuted: shown false, with a witness.

status_detail.description: What the status rests on, in one or two sentences: which checker, how many cells, what was re-run.

cells.description: The cells the claim holds on, as the note states them: 'every cell', 'every cell with all extents at least two', 'cubic cells of side 4 to 8', a list.

cells_list.description: Optional machine-readable list of the specific cells (a, b, c) a computational claim was run on.

hypotheses.description: Standing hypotheses not repeated in the statement (frozen, odd, every hole oriented, ...).

depends_on.description: Claim identifiers this claim's proof uses, in this or another manifest. Empty for definitions and for certificate campaigns that rest on nothing but the encoding.

supersedes.description: An earlier claim this one replaces or corrects.

path.description: Path in the published repository, or in the source repository if not published (then 'private:' prefix). May be a directory or a glob pattern when a campaign has many files; a validator then requires at least one match.

regenerate.description: The command that regenerates this artefact from the scripts, with its environment.

declaration.description: The fully qualified name of the formal statement.

status.description: stated: the statement compiles with the proof left open. proved: no sorry, axioms listed.

project.description: Path of the Lake or Isabelle project.

written_by.description: Who wrote the proof or ran the computation: a model with its agent name, or a person.

checked_by.description: Independent readers, agents or people, that read the argument or the encoding with their own programs; empty if none. Mechanical checkers and second methods go under cross_checks.

cross_checks.description: Mechanical or methodological cross-checks that are not a reading: a proof checker (drat-trim, the Lean kernel), a second enumerator, a second implementation, an exact re-run of a sample.

human_read.description: Whether a person has read the proof line by line.

date.description: Date the claim reached its current status.

log.description: Where in the project's log the claim and its verification are recorded.

notes.description: Anything a reader taking this claim out of context must know: a hypothesis that is easy to miss, a correction's history, what the claim does not say.
